notes.agrum: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.genfer: Genfer answers dice2genfer.py's translation of the Dice program in floating point, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.geni: Geni computes in single precision and prints seven decimals, so differences of up to 5e-8 from the reference are its print precision.
notes.libdai: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pgmpy: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pluck: The time is the whole process's, with Julia loading Pluck; the tables take Pluck's own time, the warm one where it ran a second time in the process, else the in-process one.
notes.prism: On the weather factory the model is Rubicon's PRISM model, not the program: the same Markov chain. The time includes the JVM's start.
notes.psi: Psi answers dice2psi.py's translation of the Dice program exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.scallop: Scallop keeps every proof of each tuple (its top-k proofs at the largest k its command line takes), so its answer is exact. The time includes tddlog's grounding of the program, which Scallop reads.
notes.storm: On the weather factory the model is Rubicon's PRISM model, not the program: the same Markov chain.
notes.tensorinference: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads; the time is the whole process's, and the tables take its own, timed as Alea.jl's after a warm-up on a small model (warm-up s): the warm one where it solved the instance a second time in the process (where the first took under a third of the limit), else the in-process one less Julia's compilation within it (compile s); without Julia's start and the package's load, with the search for a contraction order.

notes.agrum: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.genfer: Genfer answers dice2genfer.py's translation of the Dice program in floating point, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.geni: Geni computes in single precision and prints seven decimals, so differences of up to 5e-8 from the reference are its print precision.
notes.libdai: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pgmpy: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pluck: The time is the whole process's, with Julia loading Pluck; the tables take Pluck's own time, the warm one where it ran a second time in the process, else the in-process one.
notes.prism: On the weather factory the model is Rubicon's PRISM model, not the program: the same Markov chain. The time includes the JVM's start.
notes.psi: Psi answers dice2psi.py's translation of the Dice program exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.scallop: Scallop keeps every proof of each tuple (its top-k proofs at the largest k its command line takes), so its answer is exact. The time includes tddlog's grounding of the program, which Scallop reads.
notes.storm: On the weather factory the model is Rubicon's PRISM model, not the program: the same Markov chain.
notes.tensorinference: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads; the time is the whole process's, and the tables take its own, timed as Alea.jl's after a warm-up on a small model (warm-up s): the warm one where it solved the instance a second time in the process (where the first took under a third of the limit), else the in-process one less Julia's compilation within it (compile s); without Julia's start and the package's load, with the search for a contraction order.

notes.agrum: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.genfer: Genfer answers dice2genfer.py's translation of the Dice program in floating point, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.geni: Geni computes in single precision and prints seven decimals, so differences of up to 5e-8 from the reference are its print precision.
notes.libdai: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pgmpy: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pluck: The time is the whole process's, with Julia loading Pluck; the tables take Pluck's own time, the warm one where it ran a second time in the process, else the in-process one.
notes.prism: On the weather factory the model is Rubicon's PRISM model, not the program: the same Markov chain. The time includes the JVM's start.
notes.psi: Psi answers dice2psi.py's translation of the Dice program exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.scallop: Scallop keeps every proof of each tuple (its top-k proofs at the largest k its command line takes), so its answer is exact. The time includes tddlog's grounding of the program, which Scallop reads.
notes.storm: On the weather factory the model is Rubicon's PRISM model, not the program: the same Markov chain.
notes.tensorinference: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads; the time is the whole process's, and the tables take its own, timed as Alea.jl's after a warm-up on a small model (warm-up s): the warm one where it solved the instance a second time in the process (where the first took under a third of the limit), else the in-process one less Julia's compilation within it (compile s); without Julia's start and the package's load, with the search for a contraction order.

notes.agrum: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.genfer: Genfer answers dice2genfer.py's translation of the Dice program in floating point, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.geni: Geni computes in single precision and prints seven decimals, so differences of up to 5e-8 from the reference are its print precision.
notes.libdai: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pgmpy: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pluck: The time is the whole process's, with Julia loading Pluck; the tables take Pluck's own time, the warm one where it ran a second time in the process, else the in-process one.
notes.prism: On the weather factory the model is Rubicon's PRISM model, not the program: the same Markov chain. The time includes the JVM's start.
notes.psi: Psi answers dice2psi.py's translation of the Dice program exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.scallop: Scallop keeps every proof of each tuple (its top-k proofs at the largest k its command line takes), so its answer is exact. The time includes tddlog's grounding of the program, which Scallop reads.
notes.storm: On the weather factory the model is Rubicon's PRISM model, not the program: the same Markov chain.
notes.tensorinference: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads; the time is the whole process's, and the tables take its own, timed as Alea.jl's after a warm-up on a small model (warm-up s): the warm one where it solved the instance a second time in the process (where the first took under a third of the limit), else the in-process one less Julia's compilation within it (compile s); without Julia's start and the package's load, with the search for a contraction order.

notes.agrum: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.genfer: Genfer answers dice2genfer.py's translation of the Dice program in floating point, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.geni: Geni computes in single precision and prints seven decimals, so differences of up to 5e-8 from the reference are its print precision.
notes.libdai: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pgmpy: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pluck: The time is the whole process's, with Julia loading Pluck; the tables take Pluck's own time, the warm one where it ran a second time in the process, else the in-process one.
notes.prism: On the weather factory the model is Rubicon's PRISM model, not the program: the same Markov chain. The time includes the JVM's start.
notes.psi: Psi answers dice2psi.py's translation of the Dice program exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.scallop: Scallop keeps every proof of each tuple (its top-k proofs at the largest k its command line takes), so its answer is exact. The time includes tddlog's grounding of the program, which Scallop reads.
notes.storm: On the weather factory the model is Rubicon's PRISM model, not the program: the same Markov chain.
notes.tensorinference: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads; the time is the whole process's, and the tables take its own, timed as Alea.jl's after a warm-up on a small model (warm-up s): the warm one where it solved the instance a second time in the process (where the first took under a third of the limit), else the in-process one less Julia's compilation within it (compile s); without Julia's start and the package's load, with the search for a contraction order.

notes.agrum: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.genfer: Genfer answers dice2genfer.py's translation of the Dice program in floating point, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.geni: Geni computes in single precision and prints seven decimals, so differences of up to 5e-8 from the reference are its print precision.
notes.libdai: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pgmpy: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pluck: The time is the whole process's, with Julia loading Pluck; the tables take Pluck's own time, the warm one where it ran a second time in the process, else the in-process one.
notes.prism: On the weather factory the model is Rubicon's PRISM model, not the program: the same Markov chain. The time includes the JVM's start.
notes.psi: Psi answers dice2psi.py's translation of the Dice program exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.scallop: Scallop keeps every proof of each tuple (its top-k proofs at the largest k its command line takes), so its answer is exact. The time includes tddlog's grounding of the program, which Scallop reads.
notes.storm: On the weather factory the model is Rubicon's PRISM model, not the program: the same Markov chain.
notes.tensorinference: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads; the time is the whole process's, and the tables take its own, timed as Alea.jl's after a warm-up on a small model (warm-up s): the warm one where it solved the instance a second time in the process (where the first took under a third of the limit), else the in-process one less Julia's compilation within it (compile s); without Julia's start and the package's load, with the search for a contraction order.

notes.libdai: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pgmpy: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pluck: The time is the whole process's, with Julia loading Pluck; the tables take Pluck's own time, the warm one where it ran a second time in the process, else the in-process one.

notes.psi: Psi answers dice2psi.py's translation of the Dice program exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.

notes.storm: On the weather factory the model is Rubicon's PRISM model, not the program: the same Markov chain.
notes.tensorinference: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads; the time is the whole process's, and the tables take its own, timed as Alea.jl's after a warm-up on a small model (warm-up s): the warm one where it solved the instance a second time in the process (where the first took under a third of the limit), else the in-process one less Julia's compilation within it (compile s); without Julia's start and the package's load, with the search for a contraction order.

notes.genfer: Genfer answers dice2genfer.py's translation of the Dice program in floating point, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.geni: Geni computes in single precision and prints seven decimals, so differences of up to 5e-8 from the reference are its print precision.
notes.libdai: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pgmpy: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pluck: The time is the whole process's, with Julia loading Pluck; the tables take Pluck's own time, the warm one where it ran a second time in the process, else the in-process one.

notes.psi: Psi answers dice2psi.py's translation of the Dice program exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.

notes.storm: On the weather factory the model is Rubicon's PRISM model, not the program: the same Markov chain.
notes.tensorinference: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads; the time is the whole process's, and the tables take its own, timed as Alea.jl's after a warm-up on a small model (warm-up s): the warm one where it solved the instance a second time in the process (where the first took under a third of the limit), else the in-process one less Julia's compilation within it (compile s); without Julia's start and the package's load, with the search for a contraction order.

notes.geni: Geni computes in single precision and prints seven decimals, so differences of up to 5e-8 from the reference are its print precision.
notes.libdai: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pgmpy: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pluck: The time is the whole process's, with Julia loading Pluck; the tables take Pluck's own time, the warm one where it ran a second time in the process, else the in-process one.
notes.prism: On the weather factory the model is Rubicon's PRISM model, not the program: the same Markov chain. The time includes the JVM's start.
notes.psi: Psi answers dice2psi.py's translation of the Dice program exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.scallop: Scallop keeps every proof of each tuple (its top-k proofs at the largest k its command line takes), so its answer is exact. The time includes tddlog's grounding of the program, which Scallop reads.
notes.storm: On the weather factory the model is Rubicon's PRISM model, not the program: the same Markov chain.
notes.tensorinference: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads; the time is the whole process's, and the tables take its own, timed as Alea.jl's after a warm-up on a small model (warm-up s): the warm one where it solved the instance a second time in the process (where the first took under a third of the limit), else the in-process one less Julia's compilation within it (compile s); without Julia's start and the package's load, with the search for a contraction order.

% The weather factory of Geni's evaluation (Rubicon's translation of
% weatherfactoryN.prism, Holtzen et al., CAV 2021; the artifact's
% bench/ICFP/weather-factory/rubicon-dice/weather-factory-N-H.dice),
% ported to ProbLog: factories, each on strike or not, and the weather, for
% $2 days. The weather starts sunny and is sunny the next day with
% probability 0.7 after a sunny day and 0.6 after a rainy one. Factory I
% starts off strike and is on strike the next day with a probability that
% depends on its strike and the weather today (strikes(I, T, S, W), S on
% or off, W sun or rain). The factories and these probabilities are
% consulted from $1. The questions are Rubicon's program's value, the pair
% of whether every factory is on strike on some day T = 0 .. $2 (reached)
% and false (second).
% The 2 factories of Rubicon's weather factory (data/geni/weather_factory/weather-factory-2-10.dice): P(factory I on strike tomorrow | its strike S today
% and the weather W today).
factory(1).
factory(2).
0.03::strikes(1, T, on, sun) :- step(T).
0.06::strikes(1, T, on, rain) :- step(T).
0.14::strikes(1, T, off, sun) :- step(T).
0.08::strikes(1, T, off, rain) :- step(T).
0.06::strikes(2, T, on, sun) :- step(T).
0.12::strikes(2, T, on, rain) :- step(T).
0.21::strikes(2, T, off, sun) :- step(T).
0.12::strikes(2, T, off, rain) :- step(T).
days(10).
step(0) :- days(H), H > 0.
step(T1) :- step(T), days(H), T1 = T + 1, T1 < H.
time(0).
time(T1) :- step(T), T1 = T + 1.
sun(0).
0.7::sunny(T, sun) :- step(T).
0.6::sunny(T, rain) :- step(T).
sky(T, sun) :- sun(T).
sky(T, rain) :- time(T), \+sun(T).
sun(T1) :- step(T), T1 = T + 1, sky(T, W), sunny(T, W).
state(I, T, on) :- strike(I, T).
state(I, T, off) :- factory(I), time(T), \+strike(I, T).
strike(I, T1) :- step(T), T1 = T + 1, state(I, T, S), sky(T, W), strikes(I, T, S, W).
some_off(T) :- state(V1, T, off).
reached :- time(T), \+some_off(T).
0.0::second.
query(reached).
query(second).

% The weather factory of Geni's evaluation (Rubicon's translation of
% weatherfactoryN.prism, Holtzen et al., CAV 2021; the artifact's
% bench/ICFP/weather-factory/rubicon-dice/weather-factory-N-H.dice),
% ported to ProbLog: factories, each on strike or not, and the weather, for
% $2 days. The weather starts sunny and is sunny the next day with
% probability 0.7 after a sunny day and 0.6 after a rainy one. Factory I
% starts off strike and is on strike the next day with a probability that
% depends on its strike and the weather today (strikes(I, T, S, W), S on
% or off, W sun or rain). The factories and these probabilities are
% consulted from $1. The questions are Rubicon's program's value, the pair
% of whether every factory is on strike on some day T = 0 .. $2 (reached)
% and false (second).
% The 2 factories of Rubicon's weather factory (data/geni/weather_factory/weather-factory-2-10.dice): P(factory I on strike tomorrow | its strike S today
% and the weather W today).
factory(1).
factory(2).

sun(0).

% The weather factory of Geni's evaluation (Rubicon's translation of
% weatherfactoryN.prism, Holtzen et al., CAV 2021; the artifact's
% bench/ICFP/weather-factory/rubicon-dice/weather-factory-N-H.dice),
% ported to ProbLog: factories, each on strike or not, and the weather, for
% $2 days. The weather starts sunny and is sunny the next day with
% probability 0.7 after a sunny day and 0.6 after a rainy one. Factory I
% starts off strike and is on strike the next day with a probability that
% depends on its strike and the weather today (strikes(I, T, S, W), S on
% or off, W sun or rain). The factories and these probabilities are
% consulted from $1. The questions are Rubicon's program's value, the pair
% of whether every factory is on strike on some day T = 0 .. $2 (reached)
% and false (second).
:- consult($1).
days($2).
step(0) :- days(H), H > 0.
step(T1) :- step(T), days(H), T1 is T + 1, T1 < H.
time(0).
time(T1) :- step(T), T1 is T + 1.
sun(0).
0.7::sunny(T, sun) :- step(T).
0.6::sunny(T, rain) :- step(T).
sky(T, sun) :- sun(T).
sky(T, rain) :- time(T), \+sun(T).
sun(T1) :- step(T), T1 is T + 1, sky(T, W), sunny(T, W).
state(I, T, on) :- strike(I, T).
state(I, T, off) :- factory(I), time(T), \+strike(I, T).
strike(I, T1) :- step(T), T1 is T + 1, state(I, T, S), sky(T, W), strikes(I, T, S, W).
some_off(T) :- state(_, T, off).
reached :- time(T), \+some_off(T).
0.0::second.
query(reached).
query(second).
